transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… thank you. I guess I’m here because I’ve just been feeling really low. Not just sad, exactly—more like this heavy, hopeless feeling I can’t seem to get out from under. I keep thinking that everything I managed to build back up after my divorce has sort of… collapsed, and I’m just sitting there underneath it. I don’t know if that makes sense.
Did this low, hopeless feeling start after a specific stressful event?

Yeah… I think it did, mostly. It started about a month ago, around when the financial stuff after the divorce really became a mess. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming everything on that, but that’s when this feeling really started hanging over me.
If the financial problems were suddenly resolved, do you think this low, hopeless feeling would mostly lift?

I want to say yes, because that would be… simpler, I guess. And I’m sure it would help. But honestly, I don’t think it would just lift completely. It feels heavier than the money problems now—like everything I built back up after the divorce has collapsed, and I’m just sort of stuck underneath it. Does that make sense?
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I’m… not totally sure how to answer that. I guess I haven’t really been paying attention to it clearly. Some things feel harder to start, but I don’t know if I’d say I’ve completely lost interest. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How has your sleep been lately?

It’s been… not great, honestly. I mean, I’m getting some sleep, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but a lot of nights I’m just lying there staring at the ceiling, going over bills or mistakes I think I made at work. And then sometimes I wake up before dawn and it feels like I didn’t really sleep at all.
Over the past month, have you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s honestly why I came in. I just can’t seem to shake this heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I built back up after the divorce has collapsed, and I’m just… sitting under it most of the time.
Over the past month, have you had much less interest or pleasure in the things you usually enjoy?

I’m not sure… maybe a little, but I don’t want to say it’s completely gone. I still sort of want to enjoy things, if that makes sense. I just haven’t really been doing much, or when I do, it doesn’t feel the same. Is that still what you mean by less interest?
Over the past month, have you been feeling worthless or blaming yourself a lot?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to sound like I’m being overly harsh or dramatic, but yes. A lot.

I keep telling myself I’m a terrible engineer, like every missed calculation or tense email is evidence that I shouldn’t be trusted. And personally… I keep thinking I failed as a wife, and that I’m just a burden to people. I know that probably sounds extreme, but it’s hard not to replay everything and feel like I’m the common problem.
Before this past month, have you ever had another period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most of the day nearly every day?

I… honestly don’t know. I’ve had rough patches before, like anyone, but I’m not sure I’d say it was most of the day nearly every day for two full weeks. I don’t want to answer wrong or make it sound bigger than it was.
Over the past month, have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I keep wanting to say it’s just stress, but it’s been pretty bad.

I’ll look at a basic drainage calculation or a spreadsheet I’ve used for years and my mind just kind of blanks. Then I sit there rereading the same numbers over and over, and I still don’t trust myself to make a decision. That counts as trouble concentrating, right?
Over the past month, has your appetite changed much?

I’m not totally sure. I haven’t been tracking it closely or anything.

I think it’s been… maybe a little off? Some days I don’t feel very hungry, but I don’t know if it’s enough to call it a big change. I don’t want to overstate it.
Over the past month, have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

I… yeah. I’m sorry, that’s hard to say.

I don’t think I’ve been, like, trying to do anything, but I have had thoughts like… it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I kept telling myself that was just a dramatic stress thought, but it got intense enough that I scared myself and ended up calling the employee assistance program.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Over the past month, have you been noticeably slowed down in how you move or speak, or unusually restless so that you can’t sit still?

Maybe more restless than slowed down, I think.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’ve been kind of… pushing myself into things. Like taking on extra proposals, calling people at work with ideas, volunteering for tasks nobody really asked me to handle. And then even when there isn’t anything useful left to do, I’ll pace around my apartment like I’m still supposed to be doing something.

Does that count as what you mean by restless?
During these past few weeks, have you had times when you felt unusually energized or unusually confident, even while feeling low?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, not in a way I’m proud of, exactly.

Before I sort of crashed, there were these stretches where I felt really wired, like everything was finally clicking and I was unusually sure of myself. At the time I told myself it was just me being productive or confident.

But I was also… more irritable than I want to admit. I snapped at people in meetings over little comments that normally wouldn’t bother me. I know that probably doesn’t sound great. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you ever had a period when your mood was abnormally elevated or irritable for several days in a row?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but before this crash there were several days where I felt kind of weirdly wired, like everything was finally clicking and I was really sure of myself.

And then other times it wasn’t exactly “happy” elevated, more like I was irritable. I’d snap at people in meetings over tiny comments that normally wouldn’t bother me. I felt bad about it afterward, but in the moment it felt… justified, I guess.

Does that answer it?
During that wired period, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel full of energy?

Yes… I did. I guess I kept telling myself it was just because I had a lot to do, not that it was strange.

For several nights I only slept maybe two or three hours, but I didn’t feel tired the next day. I actually felt pretty sharp, like I could just keep working. At the time sleep felt kind of… inefficient, like something that was getting in the way. That sounds bad when I say it out loud, doesn’t it?
During that wired period, did you feel more capable or important than usual?

Yeah… I did, though I’m a little embarrassed saying it that way.

At the time it didn’t feel like I was being unrealistic. It felt like I could just… outthink everything. Like I could fix my finances, rescue a couple of difficult projects at work, and somehow turn myself into this sustainability expert all at the same time.

I know that probably sounds grandiose now. Back then it felt more like confidence, like I was finally seeing the whole picture. Is that what you mean?
During that wired period, did it cause major problems in your life—like getting you into serious trouble at work, leading to hospitalization, or making other people think you were out of control?

Yeah… I guess it did cause real problems. I don’t like saying it that bluntly, because I kept telling myself I was just under pressure and trying to fix things.

But at work I was making some questionable calls, and I wasn’t handling meetings well. I was kind of falling apart in them, and my supervisor ended up taking me off active project decisions for a while.

And at home… I stopped keeping up with basic routines. It got bad enough that I was sent to the emergency department because I didn’t feel safe with my thoughts. I’m sorry, I know that’s a lot—I’m trying to be honest about it.
During that wired period, were you talking much more than usual?

I’m not totally sure how to judge that, honestly.

I don’t remember thinking, “I’m talking nonstop,” or anything like that. I mean, I probably was more… animated in conversations, maybe more eager to explain things, but I don’t know if it was dramatically more than usual. No one specifically said to me, “you’re talking too much,” at least not that I remember.

Does that answer it, or are you asking more like whether people couldn’t interrupt me?
How many days in a row did that wired or unusually irritable period last?

I think it was… about two weeks, all told.

I kept trying to tell myself it was just a rough stretch or work stress, but the whole out-of-control pattern—being really wired and then crashing—was going on for roughly two weeks in a row. Does that sound like the kind of timeframe you’re asking for?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: The out-of-control shift from being intensely wired to crashing has been going on for about two weeks.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the wired or unusually irritable period lasted, which directly matches the duration item.

patient.answer:
I think it was… about two weeks, all told.

I kept trying to tell myself it was just a rough stretch or work stress, but the whole out-of-control pattern—being really wired and then crashing—was going on for roughly two weeks in a row. Does that sound like the kind of timeframe you’re asking for?

inference.note: History now supports a manic episode: ~2 weeks of abnormally energized/irritable mood with decreased need for sleep, grandiosity/inflated confidence, increased goal-directed activity/restlessness, occupational impairment, and ED evaluation; current episode is depressive. This rules against unipolar depressive disorders and adjustment disorder as primary.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a distinct approximately 2-week period of abnormally elevated/irritable and energized mood with decreased need for sleep, grandiosity, increased goal-directed activity/restlessness, and significant impairment requiring removal from project decisions and emergency department evaluation, followed by a current major depressive episode with hopeless mood, guilt/worthlessness, insomnia, impaired concentration, and passive death wishes. This supports bipolar disorder rather than a purely stress-related or unipolar depressive condition.
